purpose: Every place where the live App Router surface and docs/route-register.json disagree. scripts/route-register-correspondence.test.ts checks which routes exist; scripts/route-gate.ts (pnpm gate:routes) checks the methods they export, the status their redirects emit, the storage buckets their prefixes name and the (route, state) pairs a browser test proves. Both fail when a divergence appears that is not listed here, and fail when a listed one is fixed or misdescribed, so this file cannot quietly drift from reality in either direction.
notAnApproval: Listing a divergence records it; it does not bless it. The register is the binding response-contract authority, so an unregistered live endpoint has no declared auth mode, response contract or policy. Each entry names what is missing and what closing it needs.

builtButNotRegistered.why: The legacy adult-subject invitation response surface. api.withdraw is registered at /api/withdraw/[token] with token pinned to the literal "session", which src/app/api/withdraw/session/route.ts implements — and which, since 2026-09-13, answers the adult confirm/refuse/delete as well as the co-parent refusal. This bare path is the pre-migration form and is defect D-081. Nothing mails a link that reaches it any more; it stays only for the tokens mailed before that change.
builtButNotRegistered.closing: Delete with the /withdraw/[token] directory once the last pre-2026-09-13 token has expired; see the permissiveDynamicSegment row.

permissiveDynamicSegment.why: The register pins this segment to two literals and marks raw-bearer forbidden. Both literals are built (withdraw/request/route.ts, withdraw/session/page.tsx), and the [token] directory is built too, so /withdraw/<any raw token> still resolves. That is defect D-081. RE-SCOPED 2026-09-13: the adult invitation mail no longer links here. It links at /withdraw/request#<token> like every other mailed token, the adult purpose activates a rights session through api.rights-activate, and /withdraw/session answers confirm, refuse and delete off the cookie. What this directory still serves is the tokens that were mailed BEFORE that change, which live up to 30 days; deleting it today would take away the rights of the people holding them.
permissiveDynamicSegment.closing: Delete this directory, the bare POST /api/withdraw beside it, and both of these rows together, once the last token mailed before 2026-09-13 has expired — 30 days by invitation.pending-30d. e2e/adult-subject-invitation.spec.ts keeps one test on this path until then, so the overlap is proven rather than assumed, and that test goes in the same commit.

unregisteredServerActionsNote: A server action is a live mutation surface that the route register does not describe: Next.js exposes it at a generated endpoint the App Router never shows, so none of the route checks above can see it and a second one could appear without anything noticing. G8.5 asks that every live surface match its register, so the surface is held as a ledger instead, compared in both directions by scripts/route-register-correspondence.test.ts. One exists today and it is unregistered on purpose, with the reason written in the file itself. Adding another fails until it is recorded here; deleting this one fails as a stale row.

unregisteredServerActions.why: The Embryo domain's Tier-2 acknowledgement (design §1.5). Its own header states the reasoning: "A server function rather than a route: it is reachable only from this domain's own pages and needs no register row, and Next.js checks the request origin before it runs." It writes one httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookie whose value is a keyed digest of the account id and the current auth session id, with no Max-Age; it writes nothing to the database and nothing to device storage, and a new auth session cannot verify it. So it mutates no durable state and carries no authority a route would have to gate.
unregisteredServerActions.closing: Nothing. This row is not a defect and is not waiting on anything — it records a deliberate choice so that the NEXT server action has to be argued for rather than merely added. If one is ever given durable writes or authority of its own, it belongs in the register as an endpoint instead of in this list.

methodDivergence.why: The registered POST body requires "required-recent-one-time-operation-nonce", and the register never says where that nonce comes from. The code answers with an undeclared GET on the same path that mints it: it checks same-origin and a sensitive account context, then calls issue_account_operation_nonce_v1 through the service role. So the mint is real, needed and load-bearing for account deletion, and it is the one verb on this path with no declared auth mode, no rate-limit binding and no response contract.
methodDivergence.closing: A register entry for the GET verb naming its auth requirements, its rate limit and the nonce response contract. Not a transcription: docs/inherit-v2-brief.md describes no issuance surface for the account operation nonce at all, and the register is derived from the brief and pinned to briefSha256, so the brief has to describe the mint before the register can.
methodDivergence.blocker: authority — the brief must describe the operation-nonce mint before the register can declare it

methodDivergence.why: The register describes the asynchronous large-export delivery contract: POST create or open-ready with a session-bound one-time nonce, and a GET that polls status with zero enqueue and zero credential. The code ships the older synchronous route, whose own comment says so — one GET that streams the whole ZIP inline under maxDuration 300. The POST half is unbuilt, and the built GET is a different operation from the registered GET, so the verb count understates the gap rather than overstating it.
methodDivergence.closing: Build largeExportDeliveryContract: the enqueue and open-ready POST, the polling GET, the principal-bound HttpOnly export cookie and the exports bucket below. Until then the synchronous GET is what exists, and it is the same 300-second finalization ceiling the brief already names as the bottleneck.

redirectStatusDivergenceNote: Empty on purpose, and checked in both directions so it cannot stay empty through a regression. The register pins all ten legacy aliases to expectedStatus 308. Eight are pages calling permanentRedirect. /signup and /login were next.config.ts entries with permanent: false, which emits 307 — a 307 asks the browser back to the dead path every time, so the alias never retires. Both now read permanent: true.

kindDivergence.why: The register pins /withdraw/[token] to the literals request and session and calls the route a page. /withdraw/session is a page; /withdraw/request is a route.ts that builds an HTML document as a template string and returns it with its own Content-Security-Policy, nonce and Set-Cookie. It reads as a page to a person, and to the codebase it is not one: it is outside the app layout and navigation, outside pageAuthContract, and invisible to the registered-page sweep in e2e/a11y.spec.ts, which enumerates pages. Its markup is hand-written, so nothing checks its headings, landmarks, contrast or focus order the way every other public page is checked.
kindDivergence.closing: It is a route.ts on purpose: it mints a rights-activation candidate and sets a cookie before any markup, which a React page cannot do in the same response. Closing it means either registering the request literal as an endpoint in its own right, with the interstitial contract written down, or moving the mint into a middleware or action so the interstitial can be a page and re-enter the accessibility sweep. The second is the better shape and the larger change.

storageBucketDivergence.why: Measured again 21 September 2026, and the superseded text below was wrong about the bucket, not just about the key shape. Nothing live writes genomes-staging. Exactly one RLS policy ever did - genomes_staging_create_once (20260831224054:201) - and 20260906133807_cutover_subject_upload_transport.sql dropped it on 6 September. Every surviving path names genomes instead: the one remaining insert policy genomes_upload_token_create_only pins bucket_id='genomes' (20260906113021:210); private.issue_own_storage_upload_v1 inserts storage_bucket 'genomes' in its latest form (20260918150000:56); upload_sessions_token_snapshot_check requires 'genomes' whenever token_jti is not null (20260906113021:32); private.authorize_storage_upload_insert() returns false when u.storage_bucket<>'genomes' (20260906113021:191); finalization copies and removes inside genomes (20260906123327:94, 128, 170 and src/lib/uploads/subject-finalization.ts:298); and the upload.staging-2h phase executor joins storage.objects on bucket_id='genomes' (20260908121949:46). A 'genomes-staging' default does exist, but on public.upload_sessions, not on genome_files, which has no storage_bucket column at all - and every live row overrides the default. So this is a bucket the migrations create and nothing fills.
storageBucketDivergence.closing: Do not add the storagePrefixes entry the superseded closing prescribes, and do not make its four coupled edits. A prefix declares the shape, filename contract, retention and disposition of bytes that are under it. None are here, so the entry would put a written contract over an empty bucket while leaving the real staging object - a bare UUID v4 at the root of genomes - still undescribed. That real gap is already on the record, in docs/register-contract-divergence.json#objectKeyShapeNotDescribedByAnyPrefix, which measured the same keys and says storage.subject-v2 declares a four-segment path nothing writes. Until the bucket is dropped by a migration, or something writes it again and a prefix is declared for what it then holds, created-not-declared is the correct verdict and this row stays. Two manifest builders still enumerate upload-session staging objects under this bucket, so since 6 September they enumerate nothing; that is filed as D-130, which also records why it is inert today and why the half that will bite belongs in the embryo-ingest work rather than in a migration now.

supersededRecord.note: Kept verbatim so the correction is auditable. Both texts were written without reading the 6 September cutover, and the first correction - 21 September, closingWasWrongAboutTheShape - fixed only the key shape and left the wrong bucket standing.
supersededRecord.why: A real bucket holding real uploaded genome bytes: genome_files.storage_bucket defaults to it, storage RLS policies name bucket_id = 'genomes-staging', and an upload lands there before single-logical-sample verification moves it. It has no entry in storagePrefixes, so the bytes users upload sit under no declared prefix shape, no filenameContract, no retentionId and no disposition. This is the sharpest of the five.
supersededRecord.closing: A storagePrefixes entry - prefix {staging_object_name}, one server-generated UUID v4 under the database CHECK above, disposition kept (the only value the vocabulary uses), and retentionId upload.staging-2h, which already exists in docs/retention.md and already names the staging object as what it deletes. Four coupled edits go with it, or the gates fail: remove this row; add genomes-staging to declaredPrefixBucketNotAddressed in docs/register-contract-divergence.json, because the two live call sites choose that bucket from a database manifest at run time so no literal names it; move the '6 prefixes over 4 buckets' sentence in scripts/route-register-correspondence.test.ts to 7 and 5; and check the declaredBucketCount expectations in scripts/route-gate.test.ts. The retention deadline is the point: today the bytes a person uploads sit under no declared prefix, so the pre-verification window has no written deadline in the register even though retention.md gives it one.
supersededRecord.closingWasWrongAboutTheShape: Measured 21 September 2026. The closing below says to mirror storage.subject-v2, whose prefix is {account_id}/{subject_id}/{upload_id}/{filename}. A staging object is not shaped like that and must not be: public.upload_sessions.staging_object_name is CHECK-constrained to ^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$ - a bare UUID v4, one flat segment at the bucket root, with no slash and no identifier in it at all. That is the better shape for a pre-verification object, because subject-v2's path embeds an account id and a subject id in the key while this one leaks nothing, so following the instruction literally would describe a path that does not exist and might prompt someone to change the key to match it.

storageBucketDivergence.why: Created as a Storage bucket, and nothing in src writes an object to it. The same literal is used elsewhere as a retention disposition target class over database rows (public.report_artifacts, public.generated_exports, public.download_sessions, public.model_contexts), so the name carries two meanings and only the row meaning is exercised. An empty private bucket is not a leak, but an undeclared one is a place for a later write to land unnoticed.
storageBucketDivergence.closing: Decide which it is. If derived artifacts are meant to be objects, write the prefix entry; if they are rows only, drop the bucket so the retention target class is the only thing wearing the name.

storageBucketDivergence.why: The bucket the large-export delivery contract writes archives into. It does not exist, which is consistent with POST /api/export being unbuilt above: the whole asynchronous export path is backlog, not a half-built one. The declared access rules — worker-write-only, authenticated list and select denied, bounded range reads only after api.download-chunk authorization — therefore protect nothing yet.
storageBucketDivergence.closing: Created with those policies as part of building largeExportDeliveryContract.

storageBucketDivergence.why: Evidence for claim and appeal review, declared with service-only access and application envelope encryption on top of provider at-rest encryption. Nothing creates it because the claim and appeal surfaces it serves are unbuilt.
storageBucketDivergence.closing: Created with the declared policies and the document-specific data key when evidence ingest is built.

storageBucketDivergence.why: Documentary review for Record-Key, claimant-Recovery-Key and keyless future-person claims, declared with named-human-reviewer-assignment access only and four retention ids. Unbuilt for the same reason.
storageBucketDivergence.closing: Created with the declared policies and the claim-specific data key when future-person claim review is built.

provenRouteStatesNote: The (route, state) pairs a browser test title proves today, out of the 288 the register requires. scripts/route-gate.ts recomputes this list from e2e/**/*.spec.ts titles and fails if it differs in either direction, and UNPROVEN_ROUTE_STATE_PAIRS in that script holds the remainder. A title proves a pair when it names the registered route path and the state id as separate, non-overlapping, whole tokens, so "empty-history" does not prove "empty" and a state id appearing only inside the path proves nothing.
unhashableAttestationFieldsNote: Request fields the register requires that nothing can honestly produce, because the artifact they attest to does not exist. D-083. `policy.jurisdiction` appears nowhere in this repository outside docs/route-register.json — not in src/, not in the docs, not in a test — so there is no published version to name and no body to hash; these bodies carry a plain `jurisdictionCode` instead. Owner decision 2026-09-13: record the divergence and keep the code, rather than author a legal artifact to satisfy a field or drop a commitment the brief made about proving which jurisdiction a person accepted under. scripts/route-gate.ts compares this list with the register in BOTH directions, so a sixth route declaring the fields fails until it is recorded here, and the day the artifact is authored and the fields are really served, every row here fails until it is removed.
unreadRequiredHeadersNote: Required headers that no source module reads remain checked in both directions. Owner decision 2026-09-22 removes both extra headers only from the embryo chunk route, whose strict cookie, live account/session, Origin and database chunk identity provide the approved authority. The legal-evidence chunk contract is unchanged and remains unresolved; ADR 0020 decision 9 does not establish an equivalent reservation mechanism there.

unreadRequiredHeaders.why: The same header on the legal-evidence ingest path, where less can be concluded: that subsystem has tables (legal_evidence_ingest_sessions, legal_evidence_fragments and six more) but no chunk table, no reserve or commit RPC and no src/lib/evidence, so there is nothing yet for a nonce to be consumed by. The embryo finding above is not carried over to it, because the mechanism that makes the nonce redundant there - the chunk reservation row - has no counterpart here.
unreadRequiredHeaders.servedInstead: Nothing yet. This route is unbuilt and so is the transport beneath it.
unreadRequiredHeaders.closing: The legal-evidence ingest slice being designed. Whoever designs it answers this header for this route on its own evidence; if it lands on the embryo answer, both rows go at once.

taskDepthCeilingDivergenceNote: Resolved by owner decision 2026-09-22: T9 has a ceiling of six in-app click/submit actions with the registered confirmation exclusions. Mailed-link and typed-URL entry events are recorded separately. The brief, register, rubric and human protocol now use the same units. The gate still compares the empty divergence ledger in both directions.
